name: Jason Crow

summary.text: Jason Crow is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Colorado's 6th Congressional District, first elected in 2018.

He served in the U.S. Army from 2002 to 2006 and later worked as a lawyer and adjunct professor; he holds a bachelor's degree from the University of Wisconsin (2002) and a law degree from the University of Denver (2009).
In the 119th Congress he serves on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence and the House Armed Services Committee.

experience.text: U.S. House of Representatives, Colorado's 6th District, since January 3, 2019.

record.detail: Introduced legislation to prohibit sale of long guns to out-of-state residents who could not buy them in their home state.

record.detail: Signed into law; improves resilience of military installations vulnerable to extreme weather and climate change.

record.title: Healthcare Cybersecurity Act
record.detail: Introduced with Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA). The bill would require the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency and the Department of Health and Human Services to collaborate on cybersecurity in the health care and public health sectors, with a liaison between the two agencies and a risk study.

record.title: H.R. 1834, Breaking the Gridlock Act (extension of enhanced ACA premium tax credits), passage
record.detail: Voted Yea. The bill extends the enhanced premium tax credit under Internal Revenue Code section 36B through 2028; it passed the House 230-196.

record.title: H.R. 12, Women's Health Protection Act of 2025
record.detail: Original cosponsor. The bill's official title: “To protect a person’s ability to determine whether to continue or end a pregnancy, and to protect a health care provider’s ability to provide abortion services.”

positions.quote: I will always fight to protect a woman's right to choose. Women should have the right to make healthcare decisions that are right for them and their families.

I introduced legislation to close the “Colorado Loophole,” which would prohibit the sale of long guns to residents from other states who could not buy them in their own home state, am vice chair of the Gun Violence Prevention Task Force, and was a proud supporter of H.R. 8 to expand background checks for all gun sales.
positions.note: Campaign site description of his own sponsored bill and support for background-check expansion; no publish date given.

positions.quote: We must fight climate change and protect the Colorado that we love. Climate change is the defining issue of our age.
positions.note: Calls climate change the defining issue of our age; support for speeding the shift to renewable energy is inferred from that.

No House floor roll call found specifically on public-lands sale (the Senate reconciliation provision was stripped before passage), so public-lands is sourced from his campaign site instead of a vote. WebSearch budget was exhausted mid-research, limiting further lead-finding for this candidate and others researched afterward; relied on Ballotpedia, clerk.house.gov, and known campaign/office sites via direct fetch instead. Second pass 2026-10-14: no new statements could be sourced. His Denver Post CD6 Q&A answers and a 2026-10-11 Denver Post profile (denverpost.com/2026/10/11/colorado-6th-congresional-district-crow-clark/) reinforce the deportation-priority, keep-tariffs and public-lands positions already coded here but do not newly address Amendment 81, Amendment 86 redistricting, or state zoning; a targeted Google News RSS search for his name against those two topics returned no article quoting him directly on either.
